syllabus_topics: Overview of computer networks and the Internet: packet switching; layered architecture, services, interfaces and protocols; physical infrastructure of the Internet.
Application layer: processes, ports, names, IP addresses, clients and servers; WWW, email and DNS.
Transport layer: error control, flow control, and congestion control; UDP and TCP.
Network layer: routing protocols; IP prefixes; intra-domain-inter-domain hierarchy; RIP, OSPF and BGP; NAT and DHCP.
Data link layer: random medium access protocols, ALOHA and CSMA; wireless networks; switched local area networks; virtualization.
Introduction to computer network security: confidentiality, integrity and authentication; TLS and IPSec.
assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of the exam grade and the project grade, each weighted at 50%. A final grade equal to or greater than 10 results in approval. Approval requires a minimum exam grade of 7 and a minimum project grade of 7. The exam grade is the best of the 1st and 2nd season exams of the current year. Students who scored 7 or higher on the project in the previous two academic years are exempt from doing the project and inherit the previous grade, or can opt to do the current year's project.
